findings.rule: Surface treatment must be compatible with material and supported by appropriate heat treatment for functional parts.
findings.reasoning: Hard chrome plating on Mild Steel (M.S.) without any prior heat treatment (hardness ~120 HB) provides a hard surface over a very soft substrate. Under the contact loads typical of a cam plate, the substrate will yield and the chrome layer will crack or spall. Additionally, no plating thickness is specified anywhere on the drawing, making the final Ø16 H7 bore size indeterminate after plating.
findings.correction: Change the material to a through-hardening or case-hardening steel (e.g., EN8, EN36, or 20MnCr5), add an appropriate heat treatment callout to achieve adequate core/case hardness, and specify the hard chrome plating thickness so the pre-plate machining dimensions can be derived.

findings.rule: A GD&T position tolerance requires a numeric tolerance value in the feature control frame.
findings.reasoning: Symbol S6 is identified as a position tolerance referencing datums A and B for the Ø16 H7 hole (D12), but the uncertain list confirms the actual tolerance value is not readable or present. Without a numeric position tolerance, the datum reference scheme is incomplete and cannot be inspected.
findings.correction: Add a legible position tolerance value (e.g., Ø0.1 or Ø0.2) inside the feature control frame associated with S6.
